cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Try It First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to test the shortcut, substitute, or questionable fix before you rely on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've tightened the kitchen tap's loose joint. You may test it before I commit myself to washing up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you turn it on? It sprayed me last time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your request for protection is approved. Wear my apron and open it slowly; I'll observe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You wear the apron and do the test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Reassignment is declined. I need that apron dry for the dishes. You may use my raincoat; I won't start until you've shown me the joint holds.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 approves protection instead of taking B requested role; A5 denies reassignment and grants a raincoat while withholding A reliance.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 past spray causes A3 apron concession; B4 reversal causes A5 refusal and a different protective offer.

relationship.evidence: B2 remembers the failed test and B4 tries to make A bear it, giving A persuasive work beyond mere orders.

heightening.evidence: B4 attempted reversal produces A5 a larger concession that still keeps B testing before A washes up.

specificity.evidence: A1 tightened tap joint and later washing establish the uncertain repair and intended dependence.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 dry-apron concern follows B4 demand that A wear it, exposing selective concern through the same testing problem.

coach2.stated: A1 joint was tightened; B2 a prior spray occurred; B4 wants A to test before anyone relies on it.
coach2.inferred: A5 clothing is offered as persuasion, not confirmation that the fix is safe or successful.
coach2.missing: No unseen repair outcome is needed because obtaining that outcome is the task.
coach2.firstDefect: No mandatory defect found in the current superior-controlled trial.

A1-B2.evidence: A1 asks B to test first; B2 asks A to do it after prior spraying.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 reinterprets B2 request as approved protection and assigns the test to B.

A3-B4.evidence: A3 apron offer causes B4 to reverse tester and wearer.

B4-A5.evidence: B4 reassignment causes A5 denial, raincoat concession and renewed wait for proof.
